compare_blocks.title: One-minute comparison

compare_blocks.body:
At a fictional charity sale, either person can speak to visitors, rearrange the stall or check stock. Their duties and experience may explain which task they take on.

The shared E concerns outward attention. T concerns the use of logical criteria in decisions. P concerns keeping outward options open to information. Neither type is defined by being talkative, good at logic or unwilling to follow a process.

For S/N, compare what each person draws from the same information about the stall. One reading can focus on what happened during a half hour of trading. Another can look for connections that suggest what a different display might change. Either person can use both readings.

### ENTP and ESTP: the stall moved into a windy corner, one move and two grounds

In this fictional example, the organisers move the stall from the entrance to a windy corner. Both volunteers have the same stock, time and authority to arrange the table. The next stall also sells handmade soap.

Both volunteers can choose the same action for different reasons. What they do first does not identify either type.

Both volunteers might move the table. One reading focuses on where visitors have been walking and how the tablecloth has been moving in the wind. Another looks for patterns that suggest a different layout might make the two stalls easier to distinguish. The contrast illustrates S/N, and either volunteer can consider both.

A different display can help distinguish the stall without addressing the wind. Stabilising the display may do little to make the offer clearer. Check the immediate constraints and what you want a change to accomplish.

In the notation used here, ENTP pairs dominant Ne with fourth-position Si. ESTP pairs dominant Se with fourth-position Ni. The two outward perceiving processes differ, as do their inward counterparts. Ti remains auxiliary in both, and the third process remains Feeling.

compare_blocks.body:
Boundary of use: the three scenes below are an invented charity sale and one domestic matter, used only to illustrate possible trade-offs. The division of work follows each person's experience, willingness and what is missing on the day, not type; takings are for business judgement and do not enter any typing.

If one person wants to change the wording and another wants to move the table, ask what each change is meant to solve. Either person can handle either task.

### ENTP and ESTP: at the sale, who takes which part

In this fictional sale, both volunteers can write the sign, arrange the display, record payments or speak with the organisers. Decide who does what based on experience, availability and interest.

The division can be negotiated on real conditions: who has handled cash before, who is willing to open a conversation with the next table, which piece is short of hands today. To learn about individual strengths, rotate once — wording this time, layout next — and review on actual performance rather than assuming one type is better.

One possible combination: one person fixes in a sentence what this stall sells, the other decides how the goods are laid out. That is a working arrangement, not a pairing of types, and the reverse division works too.

To check business judgement, keep a sheet by the stall: footfall estimates, number of sales and takings at three whole hours, plus three lines for each adjustment — what signal was seen before it, what reason was written down at the time, what was expected to happen. Afterwards, see whether the expectation appeared. This checks how accurate your own judgement was; it cannot prove cause, and cannot be read backwards into type — selling well does not mean any particular type.

### ENTP and ESTP: a customer says the total is wrong

In this fictional example, a customer returns with two bags of soap and says the total is five too high. Both volunteers have the same receipt and price cards. Either can verify the charge, explain what the records show and address any confirmed mistake.

One reading looks for a pattern in the labels that could explain repeated confusion. Another checks the documented price and the amount charged for this purchase. That illustrates S/N without assigning either kind of evidence to one person.

Resolving the customer’s concern and checking whether the signs need revision are separate tasks. Repeated questions may warrant a review of the labels, but do not by themselves establish what caused the confusion.

### ENTP and ESTP: the neighbour's kitchen leak reaches your ceiling

In this fictional household, someone notices signs of a leak near the ceiling. The occupants leave assessment and repairs to building staff or qualified professionals. The example concerns the information they can pass on safely.

Both occupants can describe the location and when they first noticed the mark. They can also ask the building manager whether reports from other flats suggest a broader pattern. Either person can use both kinds of information.

Whether someone reports a specific observation or asks about a wider pattern cannot identify either type.

Report what is known and what is still uncertain. The building manager can decide what needs checking. This exercise illustrates how to organise information, without asking either occupant to investigate the leak.

compare_blocks.body:
Either type can suggest a new layout or check whether a table is stable. Practical skill and creativity do not follow from the second letter.

The second misread comes from how much someone talks. Either type can strike up a conversation with a stranger and either can go silent once tired. How lively the stall is, is not a reading of the second letter.

The third ties type to proficiency. Talking well and reading a room are both trained; a stall that sells relies on both, and neither is the property of one type.

The fourth takes the order of moves as evidence. The same act of moving a table can come from having just watched the crowd, or from wanting to test a new layout; the same change of wording can be forced by the next stall or long intended. Order follows role, division, experience, deadline and information, and cannot be turned round to name a type.

The fifth mistake is inferring character from a function's position. Both stacks put Ti in the auxiliary position and Fe in the third position. That overlap describes the model's emphasis without predicting how either person reasons through a task or whether they enjoy an argument.
